pharm: Noradrenergic and specific serotonergic antidepressant; central presynaptic alpha-2 adrenergic antagonist with 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 blockade
tags: Boxed warning: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors
quick: 15 mg once daily at bedtime; range 15-45 mg/day
With or without food (minimal food effect)
Use only if clearly needed; limited human data
May pass into milk; monitor infant for sedation/poor feeding
Reduce dose in moderate-severe impairment (clearance reduced)
Suicidality, mood, CBC if infection signs, weight, lipids, sodium
summary: Mirtazapine is a tetracyclic antidepressant (NaSSA) for major depressive disorder in adults. It is usually started at 15 mg once daily in the evening and titrated up to a maximum of 45 mg/day. Sedation and increased appetite/weight gain are prominent (sedation often more pronounced at lower doses). It is contraindicated with MAOIs because of serotonin syndrome risk and carries a boxed warning for increased suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients.

dosage.d: Start 15 mg once daily; titrate up to a maximum of 45 mg/day
dosage.t: Once daily, preferably in the evening before sleep
dosage.n: Do not change dose at intervals shorter than 1 to 2 weeks to allow adequate evaluation of response

dosage.d: Start at the low end of the dosing range (e.g., 15 mg); titrate cautiously
dosage.n: Reduced clearance; greater risk of over-sedation, confusion, and hyponatremia

dosage.d: A dosage decrease may be needed; clearance reduced ~30% (GFR 11-39) to ~50% (GFR <10)
dosage.n: Plasma levels may be increased; titrate with clinical monitoring

dosage.d: A dosage decrease may be needed; oral clearance reduced ~30%
dosage.n: Use with caution; monitor for transaminase elevations

dosage.d: Gradually reduce the dose rather than stopping abruptly
dosage.n: Abrupt stop or dose reduction may cause discontinuation symptoms

admin: Administer orally once daily, preferably in the evening prior to sleep
May be taken with or without food (presence of food has minimal effect on absorption)
Screen for personal or family history of bipolar disorder, mania, or hypomania before starting
Allow at least 14 days between stopping an MAOI and starting mirtazapine, and at least 14 days after stopping mirtazapine before starting an MAOI
When discontinuing, reduce the dose gradually rather than stopping abruptly whenever possible
Adjust dose for concomitant strong CYP3A inducers/inhibitors or cimetidine as needed
moa: The exact mechanism in major depressive disorder is unclear. Mirtazapine acts as an antagonist at central presynaptic alpha-2 adrenergic inhibitory autoreceptors and heteroreceptors, enhancing central noradrenergic and serotonergic neurotransmission. It also antagonizes serotonin 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 receptors, histamine H1 receptors (contributing to prominent somnolence and weight gain), peripheral alpha-1 adrenergic receptors (orthostatic hypotension), and muscarinic receptors.

absolute: Concomitant use of MAOIs (including linezolid or IV methylene blue) or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI - risk of serotonin syndrome

Known hypersensitivity to mirtazapine or any of the excipients (severe skin reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported)
relative: History of mania/hypomania or bipolar disorder
Untreated anatomically narrow angles (angle-closure glaucoma risk)
Conditions or drugs predisposing to QTc prolongation
Conditions predisposing to hyponatremia (elderly, volume depletion, diuretics)
Cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease, history of low white cell count
monitor: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors and clinical worsening, especially in pediatric and young adult patients and early in treatment or after dose changes (boxed warning)
Signs of infection with low white blood cell count (sore throat, fever, stomatitis) - possible agranulocytosis
Signs and symptoms of serotonin syndrome
Weight, appetite, and metabolic parameters (cholesterol, triglycerides)

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Animal reproduction studies in rats and rabbits at up to 20 and 17 times the maximum recommended human dose (mg/m2 basis) showed no teratogenic effects, but in rats there were increased post-implantation losses, increased pup deaths in the first 3 days of lactation, and decreased pup birth weights at doses about 20 times the MRHD (not at 3 times). Because animal studies are not always predictive, use mirtazapine during pregnancy only if clearly needed and after weighing the risks of untreated maternal depression.
lact: Mirtazapine may be excreted in human breast milk. Exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman, and monitor the breastfed infant for sedation, irritability, and poor feeding or weight gain. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding alongside the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effects on the infant.
renal: Total body clearance of mirtazapine is reduced approximately 30% in patients with GFR 11 to 39 mL/min/1.73 m2 and approximately 50% in patients with GFR <10 mL/min/1.73 m2. Plasma levels may be increased in moderate to severe renal impairment, so a dosage decrease may be needed with clinical monitoring. Mirtazapine is substantially excreted by the kidney (~75%).
hepatic: Following a single 15 mg oral dose, oral clearance of mirtazapine was decreased by approximately 30% in patients with hepatic impairment compared with normal hepatic function. Plasma levels may be increased; a dosage decrease may be needed. Use with caution and monitor for clinically significant transaminase elevations.

major: MAOIs - including selegiline, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid, phenelzine, linezolid, IV methylene blue (contraindicated; serotonin syndrome)
Other serotonergic drugs - SSRIs, SNRIs, triptans, tricyclic antidepressants, fentanyl, lithium, amphetamines, St. John's Wort, tramadol, tryptophan, buspirone (serotonin syndrome; monitor closely)
CNS depressants and alcohol / benzodiazepines (e.g., diazepam, alprazolam) - additive cognitive and motor impairment; avoid concomitant use
moderate: Strong CYP3A inhibitors - itraconazole, ritonavir, nefazodone (increase mirtazapine levels; decrease dose if needed)
Strong CYP3A inducers - carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampin (decrease mirtazapine levels; increase dose if needed)
Cimetidine - CYP1A2/2D6/3A inhibitor (increases mirtazapine levels; decrease dose if needed)
Drugs that prolong the QTc interval (additive QT prolongation/torsades risk)
minor: Warfarin - mirtazapine 30 mg/day caused a small statistically significant increase (~0.2) in INR; monitor INR
interactions.food: Food in the stomach has minimal effect on the rate and extent of absorption; may be taken with or without meals.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; alcohol increases the cognitive and motor impairment produced by mirtazapine.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate cholesterol and triglycerides and hepatic transaminases; may modestly increase INR in patients on warfarin.

common: Somnolence / sedation (often more pronounced at lower doses)
serious: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors (especially in pediatric and young adult patients)
rare: Severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, erythema multiforme, bullous dermatitis)
emergency: Serotonin syndrome (agitation, hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability)
Agranulocytosis presenting with sore throat, fever, stomatitis, or signs of infection
Severe skin reaction (Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis)
New or worsening suicidal ideation or behavior

monitoring: Suicidal ideation and clinical worsening, especially during initiation and dose changes (boxed warning)
Mood and emergence of mania/hypomania; screen for bipolar disorder before starting
Signs of infection with CBC (sore throat, fever, stomatitis) - discontinue and monitor closely if agranulocytosis suspected
Signs and symptoms of serotonin syndrome
Body weight and appetite; cholesterol and triglycerides
Serum sodium in patients at risk for hyponatremia (elderly, diuretics, volume depletion)
Liver function tests in patients with hepatic impairment or symptoms
INR in patients on warfarin; ECG/QTc when used with QT-prolonging drugs or in at-risk patients
counsel: Watch for and report emergence of suicidal thoughts or worsening mood, especially early in treatment and after dose changes
Take in the evening before sleep; expect drowsiness - use caution with driving or operating machinery
Expect possible increased appetite and weight gain; follow diet and activity advice
Report sore throat, fever, mouth sores, or signs of infection promptly
Report symptoms of serotonin syndrome immediately
Avoid alcohol and other sedating medicines
Do not stop abruptly; taper under medical supervision to avoid discontinuation symptoms
Tell the clinician about pregnancy, breastfeeding, and all other medicines (especially MAOIs and serotonergic drugs)
pk: Antidepressant effect over 1-2 weeks or more; sedation within hours
Peak plasma concentration in about 2 hours; steady state in ~5 days
About 20 to 40 hours (mean ~26 h males, ~37 h females)
Store at 25C (77F); excursions permitted 15-30C (59-86F); protect from light and moisture
pearls: Sedation is often greater at lower doses (15 mg) than at higher doses, because increased noradrenergic drive at higher doses partly offsets H1-mediated sedation
Prominent appetite stimulation and weight gain can be useful in patients with poor appetite or weight loss
Absolute oral bioavailability about 50%; ~85% protein bound; substantially renally eliminated (~75% urine, ~15% feces)
Females and the elderly have longer half-lives and reduced clearance - start low and titrate cautiously

At 75 mg (1.67 times the maximum dose) mirtazapine did not prolong QTc to a clinically meaningful extent, but QT prolongation and torsades have been reported in overdose and with QT-prolonging combinations
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual once-daily evening schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Reported signs and symptoms of mirtazapine overdose alone include disorientation, drowsiness, impaired memory, and tachycardia. Serious outcomes including fatalities may occur at higher-than-recommended doses, especially with mixed overdoses, and QT prolongation and torsades de pointes have been reported. There is no specific antidote; provide supportive care and cardiac monitoring. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222) for current recommendations.
